passages.note: Operative section preempts local minimum lot sizes, setbacks, lot coverage and design rules — the V2 refined deregulation case: on-question but direction-only, silent on public housing, rent rules and subsidies.

Her quoted words praise her deregulation bill and oppose 'big government overreach' but do not reject public housing, binding rules or subsidies; the release's account of her sponsorship is context only.

rows.reasoning: Bolick prime-sponsored and voted Aye on SB 1229 (2025), which bars municipalities from enforcing minimum lot sizes, setbacks and design rules; that is cutting "the regulations and zoning limits that block private building" but one deregulation law cannot show she would "rely on the market" with nothing more. Her own words ("protects private property rights from big government overreach") show the market side but do not exclude subsidies and tax breaks, so the rungs on that side are not separated.
